findings.title: A search row with a long result or a long unbroken query overflows and is cut by the card; a long source overflows its chip.
findings.scenario: Row {source:'semantic-scholar', text:'https://arxiv.org/abs/...150 chars no space', result:'closed form'}: the query paints over the result and past the card edge. Row with a result sentence of about 180 characters: the query column collapses to width 0 and the result runs 458 px past the card, where Card's overflow-hidden cuts it. The reader loses the text with no scrollbar and no title.
findings.evidence: I built the branch CSS (vite build --outDir /tmp/lumen-review/dist) and measured the exact class strings from parts.tsx 148-165 in headless Chrome at 1280 px. Card right edge = 800. Long token: text1 clientWidth 585, scrollWidth 1087. Long result: text2 width 0 (height 80), res2 left 121 right 1258 (shrink-0, no wrap limit). Chip 'semantic-scholar': clientWidth 62, scrollWidth 76, height 38 (wraps to two lines and still overflows w-16). The spec does it with `grid-template-columns: 3.4rem minmax(0,1fr) auto` and `.q {overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap}` (docs/spec/index.html 391-395). Fix direction: `truncate` or `break-words` on the text span, a max width plus truncate on the result, truncate on the chip.

findings.title: The output block has no height limit: a 500-line output makes one step 10 000 px tall and pushes the composer off the screen.
findings.scenario: A run step with detail.output of 500 lines. The <pre> grows to its full height. The Card has min-h-96 and no max height, and the stream is not a scroll area, so the reply, every later step, and the composer sit about 10 000 px down the document.
findings.evidence: Headless Chrome, same harness: pre with 500 lines, one of them 3000 characters: width 750 (clientWidth 750, scrollWidth 25369, so overflow-x-auto works and the long line does not widen the page; document scrollWidth stayed 1280). Height 10016 px, card height 10211 px. The code is `<pre className="mt-2 overflow-x-auto rounded-sm bg-sunken ...">` with no max-h-* and no overflow-y. The spec keeps the stream in `.sessCol > .scroll {flex:1 1 auto; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto}` with the composer as a fixed foot (index.html 331-333); Session.tsx 178-186 has `min-h-96` and a plain `flex-1` div.

findings.title: The page marks the 'nothing' row with colour only.
findings.scenario: A user who cannot tell amber from grey, or a screen reader user, reads a search with four rows. The empty row is the one the spec calls 'the row that matters'. Nothing but hue separates it: same weight, same size, no text, no aria label. The word 'nothing' is only there if the worker happens to write it in row.result.
findings.evidence: Code: `row.empty ? 'border-decide text-decide' : 'border-rule-strong text-faint'` and `row.empty ? 'text-decide' : 'text-muted-foreground'`. Computed in Chrome: empty result colour rgb(138,96,8), normal rgb(89,100,111), font-weight 400 for both. The spec adds weight as a second carrier: `.srchRow.hit .r { color: var(--decide); font-weight: 600; }` (index.html 403). Fix direction: font-semibold on the empty result, and a visually hidden 'found nothing' or aria-label on the row.

findings.title: After a reconnect the findings list can lag behind the steps, because session.snapshot carries no findings and the page reads the findings list once.
findings.scenario: The socket drops while a reader records a finding. The socket returns, session.snapshot replaces tasks and steps, and the stream now shows the reader's reply 'Recorded one finding for ...'. The FINDINGS panel and its count still show the old list until a full page load. Pre-existing behaviour (Session.tsx is not in this diff), but this branch is the one that makes steps rich enough for the mismatch to show.
findings.evidence: Reducer run in node: state with 1 finding, apply session.snapshot -> 'after snapshot findings 1 steps 0': the snapshot branch is `{ ...state, snapshot: event.snapshot }`, findings untouched. SessionSnapshot has no findings field (packages/contracts/src/sessions.ts). The findings fetch effect depends on `[sessionId, projectId]` only, which do not change on reconnect. api.ts 200-203 states 'The events missed while the socket was down are never replayed'. kernel.open publishes only the snapshot (routes.ts 68). Fix direction: read `${base}/findings` again when stream goes from not-open to 'open'; the merge at Session.tsx 92-97 already handles duplicates.

findings.title: Fidelity: what spec page 04 shows that the page can draw today and does not.
findings.scenario: Compared block by block against docs/spec/index.html 1263-1440. (a) Composer, right button: the spec has Stop (aria-label 'Stop') while the session runs; the page has Send only. `session.stop` is in ClientCommand and Kernel.stop exists, so no contract change is needed. (b) Header: the spec adds '/ <agent>' to the breadcrumb when a child task is open (data-agentcrumb, script line 1772); the page header never names the task shown. (c) Stream is a scroll area with the composer pinned at the foot; the page grows the document (Session.tsx 178). (d) THINKING has a ground background (`.turn-think {background: var(--ground)}`), the page has the left border only. REPLY has `border-left: 3px solid var(--ink)` and an ink label; the page has no left border and a text-keep (green) label. (e) A child task's first block is labelled 'task'; the page writes 'to <agent>' (parts.tsx 87). (f) A tool step with no duration shows 'tool call' at the right (save, record); the page shows nothing. (g) Money: the spec writes '$0.01', the page writes '$0.0100' on every step and in the header (`toFixed(4)`), and a step with cost {dollars:0} draws '$0.0000' because `detail?.cost ?` tests the object, not the amount. (h) DELEGATED: '3 in parallel' is a busy status chip in the spec, a plain faint eyebrow here. (i) Search query is one line with ellipsis in the spec.
findings.evidence:
Spec lines quoted: 1291 `search ... 6 s · $0.01`; 1300 `delegated ... 3 in parallel`; 1311/1323 `save`/`record` with `tool call`; 1346 `
task
`; 1412-1416 composer with `class="act stop" aria-label="Stop"`; CSS 478-485 turn-you / turn-think / turn-reply. Page: parts.tsx 123-129 (thinking, no bg), 204-210 (reply, `text-keep`, no border), 33-35 money, 136 cost test, 318 Send button.

findings.title: Fidelity: what spec page 04 shows that needs data the contract does not carry.
findings.scenario: (a) FINDINGS: each finding has a status chip ('confirmed' / 'open') and a second text that opens on click (findingHTML, index.html 2101-2107). Finding has id, sessionId, taskId, text, createdAt only; the page puts the agent name where the spec puts the status. (b) SAVE and RECORD blocks: rows with a dashed chip ('file', 'finding'), and a green bold result ('+28', 'confirmed'). StepRow can carry the three texts today, but has no field for the row tone (`.r.add` keep) or the dashed chip; only `empty`. (c) Rail panels 'This project · 1 session · replay' and 'Files · count · list': the snapshot has neither session count nor files; Files is the steering slice. (d) Thinking text streams (data-stream) and search rows arrive one at a time with a wait mark; a Step arrives whole, and there is no step update event. (e) Reply text has bold, code and subscript; Step.text is a plain string. (f) CALL TREE: the spec row is glyph, name, state; the page matches. Per-task cost is in a title tooltip only, which keyboard and touch users cannot reach; the data is there.
findings.evidence: packages/contracts/src/sessions.ts: StepRow {source,text,result,empty?}; Finding {id,sessionId,taskId,text,createdAt}; SessionSnapshot has session, tasks, steps, totals, spend. Spec: REC1 rows `['finding','3-stack-sortable is A134664','confirmed','f1']` (2092), `.srch.rec .src {border-style:dashed}` (401), rail sections at 1421-1434.

findings.title: When detail.tool is set and the text prefix does not match the label pattern, the body repeats the tool name.
findings.scenario: A worker writes appendStep(id,'tool','web_search: pop-stack', {tool:'web_search'}) or 'Search: ...'. The label comes from detail.tool, but the body comes from toolLabel(step.text), whose regex allows only [a-z0-9-]. The block reads 'WEB_SEARCH' over 'web_search: pop-stack'.
findings.evidence: Ran tree.ts in node: toolLabel('web_search: x') -> {label:'tool', body:'web_search: x'}; toolLabel('Search: x') -> {label:'tool', body:'Search: x'}. parts.tsx 141 uses `detail?.tool ?? parsed.label`, 144 uses `parsed.body` always. Fix direction: when detail.tool is set, strip a leading `${detail.tool}:` from the text.

findings.title: took() writes '1000 ms' for 999.5 to 999.99 ms.
findings.scenario: durationMs 999.6 (Date.now differences are integers, so this needs a worker that reports a fractional time). The branch test is on the raw value, the text is from the rounded value.
findings.evidence: Ran in node: took(999.6) -> '1000 ms'. Other boundaries are right: 0 -> '0 ms', 1000 -> '1 s', 9950 -> '9.9 s', 9999 -> '10 s', 59999 -> '1 min 0 s', -5 -> '0 ms'. Missing durationMs gives no receipt part (parts.tsx 135 tests `=== undefined`), which is right; durationMs 0 draws '0 ms'.

checked_and_fine: Theme classes: text-faint, border-rule-strong, bg-sunken, text-decide, border-decide, text-keep, text-gap, text-ink, text-body all have a --color-* token in apps/web/src/styles/theme.css (lines 115-126) and each appears once in the CSS I built from the branch.
UI rules: no `style=` and no hex colour in apps/web/src/pages/session/*.tsx (grep); controls come from @/ui/button, @/ui/input, @/ui/card; no new dependency in the diff.

Web checks on the branch: vitest apps/web 22 tests pass; eslint (with jsx-a11y) on pages/session and core/api.ts is clean; tsc -p apps/web --noEmit is clean. There is no component test for parts.tsx; only tree.ts and the reducer have tests.

Reducer, duplicate detection: a second step.appended with the same (taskId,index) leaves 1 step (ran it). Order is arrival order, not index order (indices arrived 0,2,1 stay 0,2,1); one ordered socket plus snapshot replace makes this safe in practice.

Reducer, the spread: `{type, ...step}` drops only `type`. With today's contract the event fields are exactly Step's fields, so nothing leaks. A future server field on the event (I sent sessionId and seq) does land in the Step object; harmless at run time and TypeScript accepts it because the rest type is structurally a Step.

Event order for a delegate step: Kernel.delegate publishes every task.opened before it writes the delegate step, so on a live socket the named children are always present when the step arrives; a snapshot replaces tasks and steps together.

childrenByStep: named ids win; old steps take the next N children that no step names (ran: old step + new step naming c,d -> [a,b] and [c,d]); detail without childTaskIds falls back to the count; a named id with no task is dropped without error; empty childTaskIds gives an empty list. Duplicates need a step that names an id twice or two steps naming one child ([a,a] -> duplicate React key); the kernel cannot produce either because appendStep rejects childTaskIds from a worker. The 'first number in the text' fallback misreads a text like 'readers of the 2019 survey', but that is unchanged from main and main's worker only ever wrote 'delegated N in parallel'.
A tool step with no detail: label and body come from toolLabel(text), no receipt, no rows, no pre. Same as main.
Long output line: overflow-x-auto on the pre works inside the minmax(0,1fr) column; measured pre width 750 with scrollWidth 25369 and no page-level horizontal scroll.

Accessibility: every button has a name (tree and delegate rows from their text, Attach and Send from aria-label, input from aria-label); tree rows and delegate rows are native buttons, so Tab and Enter reach them; aria-current='true' on the selected tree row is a valid value. The tree row's accessible name includes the box-drawing glyphs, which is a cosmetic point only.
The browser adds no money: step cost, ownCost, totals and spend are all drawn from server values; money() only formats.
No duplicate YOU block: Kernel.start does not write a 'you' step for the first turn, so the title block is the only one; Kernel.say writes one for later turns.
Composer while offline: the submit button is disabled, and a form whose default button is disabled does not submit on Enter, so text is not lost to a closed socket.
